feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Africa: Trading in yuan
entry.summary: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.

entry.title: Bagel makers, lovers and critics converged in New York for best bagel contest
entry.summary: The best bagel contest in New York City last weekend drew competitors from around the world, and of course lots of hometown bagel makers and critics.

entry.title: Brain cell mapping lays groundwork for better treatments for conditions like dementia
entry.summary: A major effort from brain researchers around the world has yielded a cellular atlas of the basal ganglia — structures key to learning and controlling motor skills.

entry.title: Questions about FAA funding roil Capitol Hill after nationwide ground stop
entry.summary: Three days after a communications meltdown led the FAA to ground planes, there are big questions about what happened and how much money is needed to upgrade the country's air traffic control system.

entry.title: A meteorite hit her home. She's showing it to Houston: 'I want everybody to see it'
entry.summary: Earlier this year, a meteorite crashed into the home of a Houston-area woman. Most of the meteor burned up, but 19 fragments were found and are on display at the Houston Museum of Natural Science.

entry.title: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
entry.summary: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

entry.title: Pope Leo XIV wraps up demanding, emotional Latin America tour
entry.summary: After visiting three countries and 10 cities, Pope Leon XIV is headed back to Rome. He wrapped up the 12-day tour with an emotional send off in Peru, his second homeland.

entry.title: If Robert Pattinson is James Bond, 007 needs to get a little weird
entry.summary: Amazon announced Monday that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond. NPR critic Glen Weldon says the idiosyncratic actor would seem to be a better fit as a Bond villain.

entry.title: In 'Club Kid' Jordan Firstman shares his softer side: 'Something more from the heart'
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Jordan Firstman, who wrote, directed and acted in the new film Club Kid.

entry.title: Pilot and journalist says fault lines beginning to show in U.S. air travel
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with James Fallows about his reporting on the safety of air travel, published in the New York Times Magazine the day before the nationwide ground stop.
